items.title: New grads have to compete with AI for entry
items.summary: A national study reveals that nearly half of hiring managers would rather invest in AI tools than spend resources training new college graduates, pushing companies to significantly restructure entry-level business and operations roles.

items.title: Class of 2026 College Graduate Hiring Report
items.summary: Insights from the Class of 2026 College Graduate Hiring Report show that 55% of surveyed companies have actively redirected a portion of their entry-level hiring budgets to AI tools, requiring business graduates to enter the workforce with immediate execution-ready skills.

items.title: What AI Skills Do Employers Actually Look For in 2026?
items.summary: Labor market research indicates that over one-third of entry-level job postings now demand some form of AI competency, with employers prioritizing practical AI literacy and workflow automation skills in business fields like marketing, operations, and HR.

items.title: 2026 AI, Automation, and the Future of Business Administration Degree Careers
items.summary: This comprehensive overview outlines how AI automation is fundamentally redefining business administration pathways, shifting graduate roles toward strategic forecasting, high-level planning, and data literacy rather than routine task-based administration.

items.title: Will AI Replace Healthcare Jobs? Not How You May Think
items.summary: While AI is replacing repetitive administrative, coding, and medical transcription tasks, it is simultaneously creating new high-touch career paths such as "Clinical AI Implementation Specialists" and "Healthcare AI Ethics and Governance Analysts".

items.title: 2026 AI, Automation, and the Future of Health Studies Degree Careers
items.summary: With over 40% of health employers now integrating automation, health studies graduates are finding career stability by pivoting to personalized medicine and health data analysis, which require a mix of clinical knowledge and tech management.

items.title: 2026 AI, Automation, and the Future of Health Studies Degree Careers
items.summary: Driven by a projected 30% job growth in medical AI roles through 2028, health and medical professionals are increasingly pursuing interdisciplinary upskilling to transition into lucrative roles like Healthcare AI Consultants and clinical-focused AI Product Managers.

items.title: Healthcare AI Hiring Trends 2026
items.summary: Recruiting data reveals that U.S. health systems are doubling their AI headcounts, with hiring surges concentrated heavily in ambient clinical AI scribe systems implementation, clinical AI product management, and AI risk governance.

items.title: 2026 AI, Automation, and the Future of Art Studies Degree Careers
items.summary: This report outlines how AI and automation are transforming career pathways for art majors by shifting entry-level roles away from routine cataloging and curation and toward high-value creative direction, digital literacy, and AI tool proficiency.

items.title: The state of the creative industry 2026: what our survey tells us about pay, burnout and AI
items.summary: Highlighting findings from a global survey of 882 creative professionals, this article reveals that while 86% of creatives are now utilizing AI, only 10% view its impact as positive, underscoring intense career anxiety and downward pricing pressure on freelance artists.

items.title: AI Is Changing Creative Work, but the Arts Aren't Disappearing
items.summary: Based on a study of national labor data and Gallup workforce surveys, this report shows that generative AI has not caused the sharp wage declines many feared for artists, instead functioning as a helpful tool for early-stage idea generation and workflow efficiency.

items.title: The Best Paid Emerging Creative Roles in 2026: From Creative Technologist to AI Product Manager
items.summary: This piece discusses the emergence of hybrid careers for creative graduates who bridge the gap between design and technology, driving a shift in hiring demand toward specialized roles like AI Creative Operations Leads, Generative Content Strategists, and Synthetic Media Producers.

items.title: 2026 AI, Automation, and the Future of Liberal Arts Degree Careers
items.summary: This report details how the rapid integration of AI is driving employers to seek liberal arts graduates who possess the digital literacy to guide human-centered tech design, ethics, and communication.

items.title: How to get tech jobs with an Arts degree: Google DeepMind and Anthropic hiring humanities students for AI jobs
items.summary: Leading AI research labs are actively recruiting humanities and arts students for non-traditional tech roles—such as in-house philosophers and ethicists—to address complex questions about machine consciousness, safety, and alignment.

items.title: Humanities Graduates: Your Future Career Path Starts Here!
items.summary: This analysis highlights how the rise of AI is generating specialized roles for humanities majors in sectors like UX research, digital storytelling, and ethical AI development, where empathy and analytical skills are essential.

items.title: Why AI is ‘resurrecting’ the liberal arts for the Class of 2026
items.summary: Career experts argue that because AI has commodified basic execution, employers are increasingly placing a premium on the "liberal arts brain" to provide strategic intent, critical thinking, and ethical oversight.

items.title: 2026 AI, Automation, and the Future of Sociology Degree Careers
items.summary: This report outlines how AI is reshaping the sociology workforce by automating repetitive data collection and coding tasks while simultaneously driving a 15% projected growth in advanced, tech-driven roles like "Social Data Scientists".

items.title: 2026 AI, Automation, and the Future of Sociology Degree Careers
items.summary: Reflecting a 22% spike in the workforce skill gap, this analysis highlights that public and non-profit sectors are increasingly offering 15% salary premiums for social science graduates who can translate AI-generated insights into ethical, community-centric interventions.

items.title: AI and the Labor Market: Revolution or Evolution?
items.summary: Drawing from a new Gallup-Lumina report, this article notes that social science and humanities majors are among the least likely to switch fields due to AI anxieties, as their foundational training emphasizes qualitative context, ethical judgment, and human reasoning—areas where AI continues to struggle.

items.title: Coding agents in the social sciences
items.summary: A survey of 1,260 quantitative social scientists revealed that 81% have integrated AI chatbots into their research workflows, with early adopters utilizing autonomous coding agents to drastically accelerate the analysis of complex human behaviors and datasets.

items.title: New grads have to compete with AI for entry
items.summary: According to a survey by ResumeTemplates.com, 48% of hiring managers would rather invest in AI tools than spend resources hiring and training recent college graduates, indicating that entry-level STEM applicants must actively prove they can utilize and manage AI systems to stand out.

items.title: College graduates face competitive market as artificial intelligence spending rises
items.summary: This report highlights that 55% of surveyed companies have redirected portions of their hiring budgets toward AI tools, creating a highly competitive market where STEM graduates can no longer rely on traditional onboarding and must demonstrate immediate technical competency.

items.title: 2026 The Future of AI Jobs for College Graduates
items.summary: Recent data from Handshake shows that 23.3% of internship listings now require AI skills (up from less than 10% in 2024), but STEM graduates with AI-focused backgrounds command starting salaries that are 25% to 30% higher than non-AI technical roles.

items.title: What Three New Studies On AI, Work And Jobs Tell Us
items.summary: Reflecting on Microsoft's 2026 Work Trend Index and LinkedIn data, this piece reports that while AI will reshape up to 55% of jobs, it has also spurred the creation of over 1.3 million AI-related roles, proving that the strongest career path for STEM majors lies in combining deep technical skills with human judgment and contextual reasoning.

items.title: Class of 2026: What occupation data show about AI and the young college graduate workforce
items.summary: While college graduates and STEM majors are heavily concentrated in AI-exposed occupations, this analysis suggests that recent increases in graduate unemployment are primarily driven by a broader softening of the macroeconomic labor market rather than direct automation-driven job displacement.

items.title: AI Jobs Surged 8 Times Faster Than The Job Market. You Don’t Need To Code
items.summary: The massive growth in AI-related job postings is primarily driving demand for non-coding business, marketing, healthcare, and project management roles where employees can apply AI workflows and business logic without technical programming backgrounds.

items.title: New grads have to compete with AI for entry
items.summary: A growing number of employers are shifting entry-level hiring budgets to AI tools instead of training raw graduates, making it essential for non-STEM and general graduates to demonstrate immediate technological competency alongside strong soft skills.

items.title: Why AI is ‘resurrecting’ the liberal arts for the Class of 2026
items.summary: AI's automation of technical and executable tasks has reversed labor market values, placing a substantial premium on the "liberal arts brain" which excels at critical thinking, ethical reasoning, and strategic oversight.

items.title: 2026 AI, Automation, and the Future of Humanities Degree Careers
items.summary: While AI automates routine administrative tasks, it is rapidly expanding specialized opportunities for humanities graduates in ethical AI development, digital humanities, and roles requiring highly adaptive communication and empathy.

items.title: Report Highlights Changing Views on Skilled Trades
items.summary: A national report reveals that AI is accelerating a generational shift toward hands-on careers, with 68% of parents rethinking white-collar stability and 76% of Gen Z prioritizing career paths that are difficult to automate.

items.title: AI-Driven Shift Sees Blue-Collar Jobs Rise as Entry-Level White-Collar Roles Slow
items.summary: As AI continues to automate cognitive entry-level desk tasks, major companies like Ford and AT&T are ramping up their recruitment of electricians, mechanics, and technicians to leverage a workforce less vulnerable to automation.

items.title: How AI Is Changing Skilled Trades in 2026 (Your Job Is Safer Than You Think)
items.summary: The physical infrastructure required to support AI is driving an unprecedented surge in demand for trades majors, specifically electricians, HVAC technicians, and pipefitters needed to build and manage highly demanding data centers.

items.title: Skilled Trades Survey 2026: How Gen Z Views AI & College
items.summary: A survey of Gen Z adults showed a significant shift in career perception, with 52% of current college students asserting that skilled trades are safer from AI displacement than traditional office-based corporate roles.
